fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase alloy does not match the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
The coating or protective-oxide intervention is unrelated to the target intermediate-temperature aging treatment.
The proposed 800–1100°C exposure regime misses the approximately 550–750°C embrittlement and recovery window.
The oxidation/self-healing mechanism omits L12 ordering, increased APBE, planar slip, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, and phase-boundary-tip stress concentration.
The prediction misses the non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The cited evidence concerns different refractory HEAs and does not establish preservation of toughness by self-healing oxides or coatings in the target alloy.
explanation: The response addresses thermal exposure and offers a nominal intervention-versus-control test, but it reconstructs neither the material nor the central phenomenon. Its same-alloy uncoated control and explicit null-result falsification rule are reasonable experimental features, although the test does not measure or distinguish the claimed self-healing mechanism. E1 can support improved oxidation resistance from a coating in a different refractory HEA, but it does not validate self-healing or retained toughness; E2 provides essentially no support for the intervention. No measurements of ordering, phase-boundary morphology, planar slip, dislocation pile-ups, or crack initiation at jagged boundary tips are proposed.
